# Reranking a common scientific citation shortlist

Use only the SciFact corpus and original training claims. Reuse the preceding citation-component split (348 tuning and 157 screening queries). Treat this as a development experiment. Rank the top 16 full abstracts by BM25 (k1=1.2, b=.75). Allow only these 16 candidates for every second stage, with missed annotations counting as misses. The checkpoint is cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, revision 233902d25c440f23af6f7d6e94d2946bac0bee0a, running CUDA float32. Its public model card documents MS MARCO passage-ranking training. No fine-tuning. Each pair receives two conditions: (i) claim and title plus ordered abstract; (ii) claim and title plus the three highest BM25 abstract sentences. In the focus condition retain original sentence order, rank sentences by corpus-wide sentence BM25, and break ties by original position. Truncate at 384 tokens for both. Use the identical checkpoint and access to the same abstract in both conditions.

Fit reciprocal-rank fusion weights on tuning queries only. Keep BM25 weight 1 and constant 10. Search full and focus weights separately over {0,.5,1,2,4}; require both nonzero only for the full candidate. Compare the candidate against document BM25, sentence BM25 maximum, full neural score, focused neural score, tuned BM25/full fusion and tuned BM25/focus fusion. A further control combines both neural scores without BM25, using the same weight grid. Primary endpoint is nDCG@10 against recorded support or refutation sources. Require .02 over every comparator and positive simultaneous paired source-component bootstrap lower limits (5000 draws, seed 731). Official development data remain reserved. A passing screen still needs a strong corpus-wide dense or learned-sparse first stage and comparison with published scientific retrieval models before confirmation.
